summary: The lecture traces the historical evolution of the Indian Constitution from the arrival of the East India Company (1600) to the Indian Independence Act (1947). It covers key legislative acts — Regulating Act (1773), Pitt's India Act (1784), Charter Acts (1813, 1833, 1853), Government of India Acts (1858, 1919, 1935), and Indian Councils Acts (1861, 1892, 1909) — highlighting administrative changes, judicial setup, electoral reforms, and the transition from Company rule to Crown rule.
points: 1600 Dec 31: Queen Elizabeth I granted charter to East India Company (100 London merchants).
1757 Battle of Plassey: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah; British gained control of Bengal.
1764 Oct 22 Battle of Buxar: Clive defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, Shah Alam II; secured Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, Orissa.
1773 Regulating Act: First parliamentary control; Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings first); Supreme Court at Calcutta (Sir Elijah Impey first CJ).
1784 Pitt's India Act: Board of Control (6 members) in England; Governor-General appointed by British Govt; Executive Council reduced to 3; separated commercial/political functions.
1833 Charter Act: Ended Company trade monopoly; Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India (William Bentinck first); added Law Member (Macaulay).
1858 Nov 1 Government of India Act: Ended Company rule; Crown rule began; Governor-General became Viceroy (Lord Canning first); Secretary of State for India with 15-member Council created.
1909 Morley-Minto Reforms: Introduced separate electorates for Muslims; allowed supplementary questions on budget.

1919 Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms: Dyarchy in provinces (transferred/reserved subjects); bifurcated central/provincial subjects; direct elections; separate electorates for Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians.

1935 Government of India Act: Provincial autonomy; abolished dyarchy in provinces; introduced dyarchy at centre; bicameral legislatures; Federal Court at Delhi (1 CJ + 6 judges); RBI established; Federal Legislature.
1947 July Indian Independence Act: Partition into India/Pakistan (Aug 15, 1947); ended British paramountcy; separate Constituent Assemblies; Radcliffe Commission for boundaries.

check.q: Which Act first established the Supreme Court at Calcutta with Sir Elijah Impey as Chief Justice?
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) introduced which major administrative feature in provinces?
Which Act abolished the East India Company's trade monopoly completely and made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India?
